basics.name: Aarti Darji
basics.label: M.S. Computer Science Student, NYU Courant
basics.summary: Researching multimodal representation learning and biomedical data science, with a background in human-computer interaction and tangible computing.

education.institution: New York University, Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences

education.area: Data Science, Honors (concentration in Psychology, minor in Mathematics)

work.name: UTHealth Houston
work.position: Research Assistant I — Analyzing Gulf War Illness in Veterans
highlights: Curated and maintained raw and processed MRI data for Gulf War Illness studies in veterans.
Performed diffusion MRI analysis using FSL and FreeSurfer for structural and tract-based insights.

work.name: Harvard Medical School, HIDIVE Lab
work.position: Undergraduate Research Intern — Agentic AI for Medical Imaging
highlights: Developed a chatbot interface for Vitessce, a visual integration tool, enabling natural language exploration of multiplexed immunofluorescence (mIF) datasets.
Built a multi-agent framework supporting biomarker exploration within the tumor microenvironment (TME) and localization of regions of interest (ROIs).
Implemented few-shot learning and a RAG approach for accurate information retrieval and structured output.

work.name: Health Data Science Lab, UT Arlington
work.position: Undergraduate Research Assistant — Self-Supervised Learning for Medical Imaging
highlights: Created an integrated search framework retrieving the most similar spatial proteomics (CODEX/PhenoCycler) imaging from an input histopathology slide.
Developed and trained a Variational Autoencoder (VAE) on HPC clusters to obtain latent spaces of patches for similarity search.
Conducted validation and ablation studies showing the potential of search engines to aid clinicians in diagnosis and treatment decisions.

work.name: Hybrid Atelier, UT Arlington
work.position: Undergraduate Research Assistant — Hybrid Design and Fabrication
highlights: Lasercut and 3D-printed molds to develop silicone samples with different micro-textures, studying the effect of haptic perception on emotion and decision making.
Built a web application with React and a Flask API to collect user responses and study texture perception of silicone samples.
Developed a layered silicone composite sensor with unique electrode designs to study new gesture creation and cross-modal correspondences.
Achieved 97% accuracy training a CNN to predict user gestures from sensor-reading heatmaps.

work.name: Controlled Attention and Memory Lab, UT Arlington
work.summary: Advisors: Dr. Matthew Robison and Dr. Pedro Maia
highlights: Wrote Python analysis code surfacing average reaction time and pupil diameter/gaze shift from eye-tracking devices across 300+ participants.
Calculated the sample entropy of pupil diameter to determine its regularity based on goal type, feedback, and reward.
